methods.notes: The device advertises with the product name at GATT handle 0x0321 reading "CC-RT-BLE"; scan by that name prefix.

device.name: eQ-3 Eqiva Bluetooth Radiator Thermostat (CC-RT-BLE)
device.notes:
The Eqiva eQ-3 Bluetooth radiator valve (CC-RT-BLE) is a hugely common European smart TRV. It has no radio but BLE, so control is entirely local: commands are written to a vendor GATT characteristic and status arrives on a notify characteristic. Firmware 1.20+ may require a one-time BLE pairing (hold the wheel until "Pair" shows).
GATT: write commands to characteristic 3fa4585a-ce4a-3bad-db4b-b8df8179ea09 (handle 0x0411); status notifications on d0e8434d-cd29-0996-af41-6c90f4e0eb2a (handle 0x0421). The product name "CC-RT-BLE" is at handle 0x0321, vendor "eq-3" at handle 0x0311.
COMMANDS (first byte = opcode):
  00                        read serial
  03 yy mm dd hh mm ss      request status + sync clock
  40 00 / 40 40 / 40 a3     mode: auto / manual / vacation
  41 <target*2>             set target temperature (value = °C × 2)
  43 / 44                   comfort preset / eco preset
  45 01 / 45 00             boost on / boost off
  80 01 / 80 00             lock / unlock the buttons
  11 ...                    configure comfort/eco presets
  13 <(offset+3.5)*2>       set temperature-sensor offset
  14 <temp>                 window-open detection config
  20 <day 00-06>            read a day's schedule (00=Sat..06=Fri)
  f0                        factory reset
Temperatures throughout are one byte = °C × 2 (decode as byte / 2).
STATUS NOTIFICATION: byte1 0x02, byte2 0x01, byte3 mode bitfield (manual 0x01, vacation 0x02, boost 0x04, ...), byte4 valve %, byte5 0x04, byte6 target temp (value/2 °C), bytes 7-10 vacation date, bytes 11-15 comfort/eco/ window config.

openness.notes: No vendor API; the protocol was reverse-engineered. Heckie75 documents the byte tables and python-eq3bt (bleak/bluepy/gattlib) implements them.

upstream_docs.covers: The full byte-level command/response tables and the status notification layout.
upstream_docs.title: Heckie75 — eQ-3 radiator thermostat API

enter_pairing_mode.notes: Firmware 1.20+ only. Older firmware connects with no pairing step at all, so a client must handle both and should not treat a valve that never asks as a failure.

procedures.basis: rytilahti/python-eq3bt, which documents the firmware 1.20+ pairing requirement alongside the GATT characteristic UUIDs used here. Not replayed against a valve.
procedures.name: Hold the valve wheel until the display shows "Pair"

steps.action: Hold the wheel on the valve head.
Release when the display shows "Pair", then connect.

exclusivity.recovery: Only one client at a time. A new client connects — and pairs, on firmware 1.20+ — independently; existing pairings are unaffected, so adding a controller does not cost the household its phone app.

pairing.notes: A firmware split rather than a device property: everything below 1.20 connects and is controlled with no pairing whatsoever, and 1.20+ may ask for a one-time pairing first. The link-layer key, where one exists, is the only thing stored — the schedule, presets and sensor offset are device configuration and survive any pairing change.

credentials.notes: Standard BLE pairing on newer firmware; no application-layer credential. There is no Wi-Fi.

factory_reset.effect: Command 0xf0 restores factory defaults (clears schedules, presets, offsets and any pairing). The device also has a physical reset via its menu.

procedures.basis: Documented in Heckie75's byte-level API; not replayed by this project.
procedures.name: Send factory-reset command 0xf0

steps.expect: The thermostat returns to factory defaults.

methods.description: Scan for the "CC-RT-BLE" name, connect, subscribe to the notify characteristic, and write commands to the command characteristic. Pair first (hold the wheel until "Pair") on firmware 1.20+.

steps.action: On firmware 1.20+, pair (hold the thermostat wheel until 'Pair' appears).
Subscribe to the notify characteristic, then send 03 yy mm dd hh mm ss to sync the clock and read status.

setup.notes: Nothing to provision beyond an optional one-time BLE pairing on firmware 1.20+ (hold the wheel until the device shows "Pair"). Older firmware connects without bonding. High confidence: two independent implementations (Heckie75 docs + python-eq3bt) agree on the GATT surface.

rejoin.notes: No network membership. A new client connects (and pairs on FW 1.20+) independently; existing pairings are unaffected.

testing.notes: Not driven against hardware by this project. The command/response byte tables are from Heckie75/eQ-3-radiator-thermostat; the GATT write/notify characteristic UUIDs and the FW-1.20+ pairing note are from rytilahti/python-eq3bt.

entities.name: Radiator Thermostat
entities.notes: Target via set_temperature (byte = °C × 2); mode via set_mode_auto/manual; boost via boost_on/off.

set_temperature.description: Set the target temperature: 41 <target*2>. The byte is °C × 2 (e.g. 21.0 °C -> 42).

raw.description: Target °C × 2. Valid target range is ~4.5-30.5 °C, i.e. raw 9-61.

sync_and_status.description: Request status and sync the clock: 03 yy mm dd hh mm ss (year is (full year - 2000)).

characteristics.name: Status notify
characteristics.notes: Status frames: byte3 mode bitfield (manual 0x01, vacation 0x02, boost 0x04), byte4 valve %, byte6 target temp (value/2 °C), later bytes carry vacation date and comfort/eco/window config.

services.name: eQ-3 command characteristic
services.notes: Write commands here (handle 0x0411). Status notifications come back on d0e8434d-cd29-0996-af41-6c90f4e0eb2a (handle 0x0421). Temperatures are one byte = °C × 2.
